The nearly century-old company delivers highly engineered aluminum products focused on strength, weight efficiency, and sustainability. Kaiser Online serves as a customer portal for quotes, order tracking, depot stock searches, and material certifications.

providers.name: Quantum Space
providers.description: Quantum Space is a space defense and orbital mobility company headquartered in Rockville, Maryland, building Ranger — a maneuverable spacecraft designed to operate across LEO, MEO, GEO and cislunar orbits. Per the company's own published material, Ranger carries up to 4,000 kg of storable propellant, uses multi-mode chemical and electric propulsion for up to 12 km/s of delta-V, is designed for a 15-year on-station operational life, supports on-orbit refueling in both directions, and exposes a modular five-port payload architecture. The company sells space domain awareness, satellite servicing, satellite life extension and on-orbit refueling to national security, civil and commercial customers, with engineering in Rockville, propulsion and integration in Hawthorne, California and Huntsville, Alabama, and spacecraft production in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Leadership includes CEO Jim Bridenstine (former NASA Administrator), Executive Chairman Kam Ghaffarian and President Kerry Wisnosky. Quantum Space publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; the only machine-readable artifact served from its own hosts is an llms.txt at the website root.

providers.name: Xwing
providers.description: Xwing, Inc. is a San Francisco and Concord, California aviation company founded in 2016 that built Superpilot, a modular retrofit autonomy system enabling ground-supervised, uncrewed gate-to-gate flight on conventional fixed-wing aircraft. Flying a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan testbed, Xwing completed more than 250 fully autonomous flights and over 500 auto-landings, and in April 2023 became the first company to receive an FAA project designation toward certification of a large unmanned aircraft system. Joby Aviation acquired Xwing's autonomy division in June 2024; Xwing retained its Part 135 air cargo operation, and www.xwing.com is now an archived marketing site pointing visitors to Joby. Xwing never published a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract; the domain's only agent-readable surfaces are the llms.txt and Site MCP endpoint that Wix generates for every site it hosts.

providers.name: Zunum Aero
providers.description: Zunum Aero is an American aerospace company founded in 2013 and based in the Seattle area (Kirkland / Bothell, Washington) that set out to build hybrid-to-electric regional aircraft. Its ZA10 program targeted a six-to-twelve-seat hybrid-electric airplane with a 700-nautical-mile range, aimed at reviving short-haul point-to-point air travel from secondary airports, and it was backed by Boeing HorizonX and JetBlue Technology Ventures. The company laid off nearly all of its staff in late 2018 and paused operations, and it later pursued trade-secret litigation against Boeing. Zunum Aero is an aircraft manufacturer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a marketing and press site with no developer program, no developer portal, no documentation, and no published machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Arctus Aerospace
providers.description: Arctus Aerospace is a Bengaluru, India based deep-tech startup building high-altitude, long-endurance autonomous unmanned aircraft (MALE/HALE UAVs) for real-time Earth observation and geospatial intelligence. Its platforms are designed to operate near 45,000 feet for over 24 hours while carrying payloads up to 250 kg, delivering centimeter-level multispectral imagery as a "zero-infrastructure" alternative to satellites. The company positions itself as a data-as-a-service provider, selling subscription-based aerial coverage for energy, infrastructure, climate, defense, and agriculture use cases. Founded in 2024 by Shreepoorna S. Rao, Arctus raised a $2.6M pre-seed round led by Version One Ventures (with South Park Commons, gradCapital, and angels). As of this writing the company is pre-product from an API standpoint and publishes no public developer surface, API, or documentation; this profile was surfaced as a Version One Ventures portfolio lead.

providers.name: Heaviside Industries
providers.description: Heaviside Industries is a defense-technology company founded in 2024 in Los Angeles, California, building autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces. Its products — MOTH (land electromagnetic signal intelligence and spectrum awareness), TYR (autonomous aerial munition), and HYDRA (autonomous underwater munition) — are designed to deliver hyper-precise strike capabilities across air, land, and sea in GPS-denied and contested environments. Named after physicist Oliver Heaviside, whose electromagnetic theory enabled miniaturized electronics, the company emerged from stealth in May 2026 with a $28M Series A. It does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: VICTUS Technologies
providers.description: VICTUS Technologies builds contested-autonomy software for autonomous systems operating in GPS-denied and jamming-heavy environments. Its PhantomNAV platform delivers precise state estimation from the gravity and inertial sensors already embedded in drones, aircraft, submarines, satellites, and ships - no new hardware required - and integrates with Palantir Foundry's AIP infrastructure. VICTUS is backed by Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes a marketing and platform site but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Wing
providers.description: Wing is Alphabet's drone delivery subsidiary, spun out of Google X in 2018, with operating headquarters in Palo Alto, California and significant operations in Australia, Finland, Ireland, and the United States. Wing designs, builds, and operates a fleet of small fixed-wing electric VTOL aircraft that autonomously pick up and deliver packages to customers' homes, and it operates an unmanned traffic management (UTM) stack used by drone pilots and aviation authorities. Wing was the first company to receive an FAA Part 135 Air Carrier Certificate for drone delivery (2019) and is an approved LAANC USS in the United States and an approved drone airspace authorization provider for CASA in Australia. Wing's commercial surface is split across two main platforms — the Wing Delivery Platform, a partner-only API and UI suite that lets retailers, restaurants, and logistics providers embed drone delivery into their own order flows (Walmart, DoorDash, Papa Johns, and others), and OpenSky, a consumer drone airspace authorization app and partner API. Wing also co-founded the InterUSS Platform open-source UTM project, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. Wing's revenue comes from per-delivery fees charged to merchant partners and from drone-as-a-service operations rather than from public developer APIs; the Delivery Platform API and OpenSky API are not openly published and there is no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Muon Space
providers.description: Muon Space is a Mountain View, California-based end-to-end space systems company that designs, builds, and operates mission-optimized satellite constellations to deliver Earth Intelligence and enable real-time compute and decision-making in space. Founded in 2021 by veterans of Skybox, NASA, and SpaceX, the company's core product is Muon Halo, an integrated technology stack composed of MuSim (constellation simulation and digital twin), MuOS (IP-based software-defined network middleware connecting space, ground, and cloud), MuCore (software-configurable instrument core), Condor (modular Condor-M and Condor-XL spacecraft platforms), and MuDash (cloud-based tasking, scheduling, and operations dashboard). Muon Space's flagship public mission is FireSat, a purpose-built wildfire detection and monitoring constellation developed with the Earth Fire Alliance, Google Research, and the Gordon & Betty Moore Foundation; FireSat carries a high-dynamic-range multispectral IR instrument capable of detecting 5x5 meter fires across a 1,500 km swath with a 50 m nadir ground sample distance, with revisit times targeted to twenty minutes once the full constellation is operational. The Protoflight satellite produced its first-light imagery in June 2025, with the first block of three additional satellites launching in 2026 and full operational capacity targeted for 2030. Other Muon Space missions support the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Space Force for next-generation weather monitoring, Hydrosat for thermal geospatial intelligence in climate and agriculture, and global security applications including missile-defense architecture. Muon Space's revenue model is mission contracting, spacecraft and constellation delivery, and hosted data services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of the Halo platform or FireSat data feed.

providers.name: TTM Technologies
providers.description: TTM Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTMI) is a leading global manufacturer of technology products, including mission systems, radio frequency components, RF microwave and microelectronic assemblies, and technologically advanced printed circuit boards (PCBs). TTM serves aerospace and defense, data center computing, medical, industrial and instrumentation, automotive, and networking and communications markets. The company reported approximately $2.9B in FY2025 revenue, operates 24 specialized facilities across North America and Asia Pacific, and employs more than 18,000 people. TTM expanded its defense electronics footprint with the 2022 acquisition of Telephonics from Griffon Corporation.

providers.name: Aleris
providers.description: Aleris was a global producer of rolled aluminum products serving the aerospace, automotive, building and construction, and other industrial end-use markets. Founded as IMCO Recycling and later renamed Aleris International, the company operated manufacturing plants across North America, Europe, and Asia. Aleris was acquired by Novelis Inc. (a subsidiary of Hindalco Industries) on April 14, 2020 for approximately $2.8 billion. The company's primary product lines included aluminum sheet, plate, and engineered products for demanding applications such as aerospace structures and automotive body panels. As a manufacturing-focused business, Aleris did not maintain a public developer API program, but engaged in B2B EDI integrations with major customers and suppliers across its supply chain. The Aleris brand has since been absorbed into Novelis and aleris.com no longer serves a website.

providers.name: Leggett and Platt
providers.description: Leggett and Platt is a diversified manufacturer that designs and produces engineered components and products found in many homes, offices, vehicles, and aircraft, including bedding components, automotive seating, hydraulic cylinders, and aerospace tube assemblies. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Aethero
providers.description: Aethero designs and manufactures radiation-hardened, space-rated edge computing systems and AI/ML software for satellites, space stations, and orbital data centers, enabling autonomous on-orbit processing of imagery and sensor data rather than downlinking raw feeds. Its NVIDIA Jetson Orin/Thor-based NxN-ECM and NxA-ECM edge computing modules, Titan and Phobos platforms, the Aether fleet-management software framework, and the AMATDT model annotation/training/deployment tool let spacecraft run AI inference in orbit. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, Aethero raised an $8.4M seed round led by Kindred Ventures in June 2025. Aethero exposes no public web API today; this profile captures the company's identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: BlueYard
providers.description: BlueYard Capital is a venture capital firm founded in 2016, operating as a small, equal partnership with offices in Europe and the United States. Managing roughly $500M in AUM, it invests $500K-$5M at pre-seed to Series A as lead or co-lead investor, backing two kinds of technologies: those that move us toward utopia and those that hold the line against oblivion. Its focus areas span computation & intelligence, engineering/aerospace & defense, biology & chemistry, and crypto. Notable portfolio companies and exits include Privy (acquired by Stripe), Groq, IonQ, Filecoin, Castelion, and Marvel Fusion. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio relationship of foundry-group and enriched from BlueYard's public website; it exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Constelli
providers.description: Constelli (Constelli Signals Private Limited) is a Hyderabad, India based defence and aerospace signal-processing company founded in 2017 by Satya Gopal Panigrahi and Avinash Chenreddy. It designs and manufactures radar systems, radar target and echo simulators, deployable drone-based radar payloads, high-performance radar processors, and IRIG-standard digital telemetry receivers for ground, onboard, and satellite telemetry. Its products serve electronic warfare and defence R&D programs globally, including India's Ministry of Defence and DRDO. Constelli raised a $20M Series A led by General Catalyst (with Pravega Ventures and 360 One). It is a hardware/systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Fortastra
providers.description: Fortastra is a spacecraft manufacturer building low-cost, maneuverable orbital defense systems designed for scalability and autonomous operation. Its spacecraft protect space-based infrastructure with autonomous navigation that detects, analyzes, and responds to orbital anomalies without relying on distant ground-based sensors. The company's open software architecture spans sensing, maneuvering, coordination, and response functions, and its hardware is validated through component testing, simulation, and orbital deployment. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.

providers.name: Galactic Energy
providers.description: Galactic Energy (星河动力航天 — Galactic Energy (Beijing) Space Technology Co., Ltd.) is a private Chinese commercial launch company founded on 6 February 2018 and headquartered in Beijing E-Town. It builds and flies the Ceres family of solid-propellant small-lift rockets (Ceres-1, the sea-launched Ceres-1S, and the larger 3.35 m Ceres-2) and is developing the partly reusable liquid oxygen/kerosene Pallas-1 and Pallas-2 medium-lift vehicles, the Eros vehicle, the Welkin (苍穹) CQ-series liquid propellant engines, and the Edge attitude and orbital control system. Its public web surface is a corporate marketing site at galactic-energy.cn carrying product pages, a launch plan, completed-mission history, a news feed, careers listings, a Chinese-language document centre of launch-vehicle user manuals (PDF), and an HTML launch-reservation form. Contract discovery on 2026-08-04 found no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API surface of any kind: every probe for OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL, MCP, an A2A agent card, /llms.txt, robots.txt and the full /.well-known/ discovery set returned HTTP 404 on every galactic-energy.cn host, and no api./developer./docs. subdomain resolves. This profile is therefore identity and domain-security only.

providers.name: GITAI
providers.description: GITAI is a space robotics company building safe and affordable robotic labor for space. It develops robotic arms, spacecraft platforms, autonomous "Inchworm" robots, and lunar rovers for on-orbit servicing, satellite assembly and maintenance, and lunar and orbital infrastructure construction, working with customers and agencies such as NASA and JAXA. GITAI operates as a B2B and government contractor and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, SDK, or developer documentation; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with the publicly observable web, blog, and domain-security surface only.

providers.name: Hermeus
providers.description: Hermeus is an American aerospace and defense company building rapidly reusable high-Mach and hypersonic aircraft for national-security missions in partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, the company applies a hardware-rich, rapid design-build-test approach to move quickly from concept to flight. Its programs include Quarterhorse, a reusable high-speed flight-test aircraft; Darkhorse, a multi-mission reusable hypersonic uncrewed aerial system (UAS); and Chimera, a hybrid turbine-based combined-cycle engine that transitions from turbojet takeoff through supersonic flight into hypersonic acceleration. Hermeus is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile tracks the company's public web, security, and corporate properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Inversion
providers.description: Inversion is a Los Angeles-based aerospace and defense company founded in 2021 by Austin Briggs and Justin Fiaschetti, building a new class of highly maneuverable reentry vehicles. Its flagship Arc is an autonomous, reusable, low-cost space-based delivery vehicle designed to store cargo in orbit and deliver it with precision to anywhere on Earth in under an hour, descending under parachutes using non-toxic propellants so crews can approach it immediately on landing. The company also develops hypersonics and space-based interceptor technology and flew its first reentry capsule, Ray, as an early technical demonstrator. Inversion has raised roughly $54M to date, including a $44M Series A led by Spark Capital and Adjacent with participation from Lockheed Martin Ventures, Kindred Ventures, and Y Combinator. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: IONA
providers.description: IONA (IONA Drones) is a UK-based autonomous drone delivery company building the full technology stack for logistics operators. Its tilt-rotor Sonnet aircraft performs VTOL from compact sites and carries up to 20 parcels up to 200 km per autonomous flight. IONA pairs the aircraft with an onboard autonomy operating system, GPS/LiDAR sensor-fusion precision landing, a SORA-aligned BVLOS compliance engine, an operations centre for real-time fleet monitoring and analytics, and a digital twin for simulation and predictive maintenance. The platform integrates with existing TMS/WMS logistics systems and targets healthcare, rural/remote, express e-commerce, industrial, and maritime delivery. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: MightyFly
providers.description: MightyFly is an autonomous air-logistics company building hybrid-electric eVTOL cargo aircraft for expedited, long-range, same-day deliveries. Its autonomous aircraft carry up to 500 pounds, travel up to 1,000 miles at roughly 150 MPH, and cut delivery emissions by around 64% versus traditional ground and air freight. MightyFly targets B2B logistics and defense delivery partnerships rather than offering a public developer platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, SDK, developer portal, or public specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Momentus
providers.description: Momentus is a U.S.-based commercial space company providing in-space transportation and infrastructure services. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Jose, California, the publicly traded company (NASDAQ: MNTS) designs, manufactures, and operates Orbital Service Vehicles such as its Vigoride platform, using water plasma propulsion technology to move satellites and payloads between orbits, host payloads, and deliver last-mile satellite deployment. Momentus serves private satellite operators, government agencies, and research institutions. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or technical integration surface; it was surfaced as a Y Combinator (S18) portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Orbital Operations
providers.description: Orbital Operations is a space-defense technology company founded in 2024 and based in Huntington Beach, California, developing high-thrust, cryogenic-powered orbital vehicles for rapid-response satellite defense, interception, and in-orbit repositioning. Its flagship Astraeus vehicle uses liquid-hydrogen propulsion with a proprietary zero-boil-off (ZBO) cryogenic storage system enabling in-space refueling and efficient payload transport between LEO, MEO, GEO, and lunar orbits. Backed by Initialized Capital, the company builds spaceflight hardware and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Phantom Space
providers.description: Phantom Space Corporation is an American space transportation and satellite manufacturing company founded in 2019 and headquartered at 1816 S Research Loop in Tucson, Arizona. Co-founded by Jim Cantrell, Michael D'Angelo and Michal Prywata, it is developing the Daytona family of small-lift orbital launch vehicles — Daytona I, II and III — alongside modular satellite buses, spacecraft manufacturing and constellation deployment services, pursuing a mass-manufacturing, fully US-based supply chain approach to launch and spacecraft production. The company acquired StratSpace and Micro Aerospace Solutions in 2021 to build out its satellite supply chain. Phantom Space sells launch capacity and satellite build programs through direct commercial contracts; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Quantum Systems
providers.description: Quantum-Systems GmbH is a Gilching/Munich, Germany-based dual-use drone manufacturer founded in 2015 by former Bundeswehr helicopter pilot Florian Seibel. The company designs, builds, and operates small electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) fixed-wing unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) for reconnaissance, intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition (RSTA), surveying, and mapping. Its flagship platforms include the Trinity Pro (mapping/surveying VTOL with up to 90-minute endurance), the Vector tactical reconnaissance drone (the de facto main small UAS supplier to the German Bundeswehr and, with 619+ systems delivered as of April 2025, one of the most-used Western reconnaissance drones in Ukraine), the Reliant long-range Group 2 ISR/RSTA platform built for the U.S. market with 10+ hours endurance and hot-swappable MOD-compliant payload bays (EO/IR, SIGINT, EW, CRPA), and the Ukraine-manufactured Sparta drone carrier that delivers two FPV drones to a 200 km combat radius. All platforms are operated through QBase 3D, Quantum-Systems' proprietary Windows-based mission planning, control, and post-processing software with integrated ESRI terrain data and direct export to Pix4D, Agisoft, Propeller, and Trimble Business Center. The Vector tactical line is built on Auterion's flight stack. Backed by HV Capital, DTCP, Thiel Capital, Project A, Airbus Ventures, and Omnes Capital, the company reached unicorn status in May 2025 as "Europe's first dual-use unicorn." Quantum-Systems supplies the militaries of Germany, the United States, Ukraine, Australia, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Romania, and Spain. There is no public developer API, REST endpoint, SDK, or open-source release for QBase 3D or any Quantum-Systems platform; integration with Pix4D/Agisoft/Propeller/Trimble is via standard photogrammetry file exchange (GeoTIFF, RAW imagery, flight logs), not a programmable API.

providers.name: Shift5
providers.description: Shift5 is an operational technology (OT) cyber and observability company that instruments the onboard serial data buses of planes, trains, and military weapons systems to deliver real-time intrusion detection, predictive maintenance, and compliance intelligence for defense and transportation fleets. Founded by former US Army Cyber Command engineers, it collects and analyzes data directly from vehicle bus networks (MIL-STD-1553, ARINC 429, CAN) to give operators actionable insight into the health and security of their platforms. Backed by Insight Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; enrichment confirms Shift5 publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Spirit AeroSystems Holdings
providers.description: Spirit AeroSystems Holdings is one of the world's largest manufacturers of aerostructures for commercial airplanes, defense platforms, and business and regional jets. Spirit designs and builds fuselages, pylons, nacelles, and wing components for major aircraft programs including Boeing 737 MAX, 787, and Airbus A350. The company does not publicly expose developer APIs; its digital operations are focused on internal supply chain, manufacturing execution, and enterprise systems.

providers.name: ASPACE International Holdings
providers.description: ASPACE International Holdings is a commercial space company founded in 2015 with offices listed in Dubai, United Arab Emirates and Hong Kong, China. It positions itself as an aerospace manufacturing conglomerate centred on the Abu Dhabi Space Eco City — a three-million-square-metre industrial cluster it says will bring together more than 3,000 partner companies across satellite manufacturing, space trade and aerospace technology innovation. The ASPACE brand is shared with Hong Kong-listed USPACE Technology Group, whose satellite-manufacturing subsidiary was renamed Aspace Satellite Technology Limited in 2023. ASPACE International Holdings has taken investment from Alpha MBM Investments and makes minority investments of its own, including a stake in the private-equity trading platform Cubin LLC announced in 2023. It is a hardware, industrial-development and investment holding business rather than a software vendor: no first-party corporate domain for the company resolves, its only verified public surfaces are a LinkedIn company page, a Hiive secondary-market listing and third-party investor databases, and it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Firehawk Aerospace
providers.description: Firehawk Aerospace, Inc. is a Dallas, Texas defense-technology manufacturer founded in 2019 by Ronald Jones, Will Edwards and Steve Edwards that replaces conventional rocket-propulsion production with additive manufacturing. Its proprietary 3D-printed solid rocket fuel, branded 3D-Ultra, is used to build hybrid rocket engines and solid rocket motors whose fuel-grain geometry is printed rather than cast, cutting production timelines from years to weeks while removing the handling hazards of traditional energetics. The company works under U.S. Army Applications Laboratory SBIR Phase III and U.S. Air Force Test Center contracts, has flight-tested an additively manufactured GMLRS-class analog, and is expanding manufacturing capacity in Lawton, Oklahoma and Crawford, Mississippi. Firehawk now operates publicly as Firehawk Defense (firehawkdefense.com); the firehawkaerospace.com domain 301-redirects there. It is a hardware and energetics manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Project Prometheus
providers.description: Prometheus (announced in November 2025 as Project Prometheus) is a San Francisco based artificial intelligence company co-founded by Jeff Bezos and Vik Bajaj, who serve as co-CEOs. The company builds what it calls an "artificial general engineer" — physical-AI models intended to automate the design, simulation and manufacture of complex physical systems across computing, aerospace, automotive production and drug development, learning from real-world trial and error rather than from text corpora alone. It launched with roughly $6.2B in funding and raised a ~$12B Series B in June 2026 at a reported $41B valuation, backed by Bezos, ARCH Venture Partners, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs and BlackRock, with offices in San Francisco, London and Zurich. As of August 2026 the company remains in stealth: prometheus.ai is served entirely behind a Vercel bot challenge, and no public developer portal, documentation, API, first-party GitHub organization, package or machine-readable contract could be located.

providers.name: Wheels Up
providers.description: Wheels Up Experience Inc. (NYSE: UP) is a leading on-demand private aviation provider in the U.S., offering charter and membership programs, commercial travel benefits through a strategic partnership with Delta Air Lines, and cargo services. Founded in 2013 by Kenny Dichter, Wheels Up was rescued from potential bankruptcy in September 2023 when a Delta Air Lines-led consortium (Delta, Certares, Knighthead, Cox) closed a $500M financing package and took a ~95% controlling equity stake. In November 2024 the company acquired the Embraer Phenom 300/300E fleet of GrandView Aviation ($105M) and secured $332M in equipment financing from Bank of America as part of a multi-year fleet modernization toward two core aircraft types (Phenom 300 series and Challenger 300/350). In 2025 it launched a new Signature membership portfolio and an industry-first integrated self-booking of Delta commercial flights inside the Wheels Up members app. Wheels Up does not publish a public developer API — its booking surface is a members-only mobile app and members.wheelsup.com web portal, with B2B operator connectivity historically routed through its acquired Avianis platform (2019).

providers.name: PowerLight Technologies
providers.description: PowerLight Technologies is an American engineering company headquartered in Kent, Washington that develops laser power beaming systems — wireless transmission of kilowatt-level electrical power over free space and over optical fiber. Founded as LaserMotive and renamed in 2017, the company builds power-over-fiber and free-space laser power links for defense unmanned aerial systems, telecom sites, temporary and disaster power, smart-grid applications, and lunar and satellite power distribution, including work under DARPA's LunA-10 program. Its products are hardware energy-transmission systems rather than software, and the company publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Radia
providers.description: Radia is a dual-use aerospace company founded in 2016 by MIT-trained aerospace engineer Mark Lundstrom, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado with a second operating base in Italy led by Giuseppe Giordo. After roughly seven years in stealth the company emerged in March 2024 with WindRunner, an aircraft it describes as the largest ever built: roughly ten times the cargo volume of a Boeing 777, sized to carry onshore wind turbine blades of up to about 105 metres, and designed to land on semi-prepared packed-dirt or gravel strips so that oversized cargo can be flown directly to a wind farm, a forward operating site or a disaster zone rather than trucked over highways it cannot fit on. Radia frames WindRunner as a deliberately low-novelty airframe assembled from existing certified technologies to shorten the certification path, targeting entry into service in the early 2030s across three markets: energy (delivering the very large blades that make low-wind onshore sites economic), defense (outsized-volume strategic airlift), and commercial supply-chain logistics. It has assembled an industrial ecosystem of more than twenty suppliers and technology partners including Aernnova, Leonardo, AFuzion, Atitech, Latecoere, Stirling Dynamics, Collier Aerospace and Maximus Air, and has raised roughly USD 128 million from investors including ConocoPhillips, Lauder Partners, LS Power Development and HCVC. Radia is an aircraft manufacturer and logistics operator rather than a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its only machine-readable public surface is the Strapi headless-CMS backend at radia.com/strapi that renders its own marketing site, whose content API is permission-locked and undocumented.

providers.name: AirMap
providers.description: AirMap was a drone airspace-management and unmanned traffic management (UTM) platform that provided airspace intelligence, flight planning, digital notice, and geofencing services for drones and their operators, exposed through a developer platform of airspace and flight APIs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07) the company appears defunct: airmap.com no longer serves a developer portal or API and now resolves to a parked Squarespace-hosted page with a mismatched TLS certificate, and the legacy developer.airmap.com / api.airmap.com / docs.airmap.com hosts no longer resolve. No live API surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Aliena
providers.description: Aliena is a Singapore-based space-technology company, incorporated in 2018, that designs and manufactures compact electric propulsion systems for small satellites. Its MUSIC plasma thruster line delivers high thrust-to-power ratios at very low power budgets with high specific impulse, enabling small satellites to operate and sustain very low Earth orbit (VLEO) for high-resolution remote sensing. Aliena is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Amca
providers.description: Amca (Advanced Manufacturing Company of America) is an El Segundo, California aerospace and defense manufacturer rebuilding America's industrial base by acquiring specialized component suppliers and expanding competition and capacity for critical parts — actuators, switches, hydraulics, pressure sensors, power electronics, and flight-control electronics. Founded in 2024 by Eli Giovanetti and Jai Malik, Amca combines design, testing, and production into a single RAPID platform across a network of AS9100D-certified factories (Electro-Mech Components, Electrocube, Aerospace Control Products, Payne Magnetics, Cal-Draulics, BC Power Systems), and serves nearly every major aerospace and defense prime and Tier 1 supplier — Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Airbus, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, Textron, BAE Systems, and the Defense Logistics Agency. It is a hardware manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: American Aerospace Advisors
providers.description: American Aerospace Technologies, Inc., doing business as American Aerospace Advisors, is a defense and critical-infrastructure monitoring company based in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. It provides end-to-end airborne intelligence systems that combine unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), airborne sensors, analytics, and communications to deliver near-real-time data through a cloud-based intelligence gateway. Its flagship AiRanger medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aircraft and InstiMaps sensor technology support pipeline and linear-asset patrol, beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) flight services, sensor integration, and aviation policy consulting. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Apex Space
providers.description: Apex Space (Apex) is a Los Angeles based satellite manufacturing company that builds productized, configurable spacecraft bus platforms for proliferated constellations across LEO, MEO, and GEO orbital regimes. Apex offers three product lines: Aries (small satellites up to 150 kg payload), Nova (medium satellites up to 300 kg payload), and Comet (large satellites up to 3,000 kg payload), and operates Factory One, a high-rate manufacturing facility in Los Angeles with the capacity to produce more than 200 satellites annually. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. Apex does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; customers configure satellite platforms through the on-site Configurator and direct sales inquiries.

providers.name: Basalt
providers.description: Basalt (Basalt Technologies Corp.) is a San Francisco spacecraft-software company building Dispatch, a simulation-based operating system for satellites that makes flight software portable across dissimilar spacecraft hardware — pitched as "Windows for spacecraft" and "Constellations as a Service." Dispatch provides a common control layer so fleets of different satellites can work together on tasking (visible, infrared, and radar imaging), in-orbit networking and telecom, signals intelligence, and monitoring or inspecting other on-orbit assets, including autonomous re-tasking for national security missions. Founded in 2023 by Max Bhatti and Alex Choi (ex-SpaceX engineers, MIT CubeSat program), Basalt is a Y Combinator W24 company that raised a $3.5M seed round led by Initialized Capital in May 2024, with participation from Y Combinator, Liquid 2 Ventures, and General Catalyst. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security. Sector: frontier-tech / space / defense.

providers.name: Cambridge Aerospace
providers.description: Cambridge Aerospace is a UK-based defense technology company, incorporated in September 2024, developing scalable interceptor missiles and sovereign air-and-missile-defense systems for European nations. Its first product, Skyhammer, is a tube-launched subsonic interceptor with a Cambridge-developed radar seeker, positioned as an affordable, mass-producible counter to drones and cruise missiles (often likened to an Iron Dome-style layered air defense). The company operates in the aerospace and defense/security sector and is backed by a venture syndicate including Accel, Lakestar, Lux Capital, Spark Capital, and the D3 fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel; it is a hardware-first defense company with no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Degla Inc
providers.description: Degla is a Y Combinator (Fall 2026) startup building an autonomous aerial intelligence layer that turns natural language into multi-drone mission execution. Operators describe an objective in plain language and Degla plans the mission, assigns aircraft, defines coverage patterns, and deploys a fleet that adapts in real time — with no waypoints, flight plans, or specialized training required. The platform targets search and rescue, emergency response, infrastructure inspection, and other critical field operations. Founded in 2026 by Aziz Hanafi and based in Boston, the company is in early access and has not yet published a public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Enhanced Radar
providers.description: Enhanced Radar is a San Francisco-based applied AI company building intelligent systems for aviation, the world's most complex transportation domain. Its work centers on pilot-controller communications, where the company owns the full pipeline from data collection through in-house labeling and quality assurance to produce high-quality aviation AI training datasets. Products include Pattern, an aviation operational intelligence platform; ATC.com, a live air traffic control radio service; and Y4, an aviation understanding model announced in February 2026. Enhanced Radar has demonstrated real-time detection of runway incursion risks and raised $7 million in May 2026. It is backed by DCVC and Initialized Capital. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: EraDrive
providers.description: EraDrive is a space technology company building compact, AI-powered self-driving modules that give spacecraft onboard autonomy — vision-based navigation, control, collision avoidance, and situational awareness computed at the edge. A Stanford Space Rendezvous Laboratory (SLAB) spinoff founded by Sumant Sharma (CEO), Justin Kruger (CTO), and Prof. Simone D'Amico (CSO), EraDrive integrates flight-proven autonomy software with existing satellite infrastructure for space traffic management, on-orbit servicing and logistics, and advanced remote sensing across commercial and defense missions. The company closed an oversubscribed $5.3M seed round in December 2025, co-led by Haystack Ventures with participation from Point Nine, Harpoon Ventures, Brave Capital, 2100 VC, and Entropy Industrial Capital. As an early-stage hardware/software company, EraDrive currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Ethereal Exploration Guild
providers.description: Ethereal Exploration Guild (EtherealX) is an Indian spacetech company founded in 2022 in Bengaluru by Manu J. Nair, Prashant Sharma, and Shubhayu Sardar, building fully reusable medium-lift launch vehicles. Its lead product, the Razor Crest Mk-1 (RCM1), targets roughly 25 tons to low Earth orbit with high launch cadence, up to 16 orbit insertions per flight, and 72-96 hour turnaround. The company has manufactured its 80kN reusable upper-stage engine (Pegasus) using a proprietary Full Flow Segregated Cooling Cycle (FFSCC) and operates a large private rocket testing facility in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu. EtherealX has raised on the order of $26M across multiple rounds, including a Series A in December 2025. The company offers launch services rather than any developer-facing API or platform.

providers.name: General Aviation
providers.description: General Aviation is a Y Combinator-backed startup (Spring 2026 batch) building a new air traffic control (ATC) system by connecting aircraft to the internet. Founded by Ben Frank, the company develops remote ATC tower technology aimed at the roughly 90 percent of airports in the U.S. National Airspace System that currently operate without control towers, giving smaller airfields an affordable path to the safety and efficiency benefits of tower services without the cost of traditional tower infrastructure and staffing. As of this profile the company operates a single marketing landing page and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: General Radar
providers.description: General Radar Corp. (GenRad) is a Belmont, California hardtech company founded in 2016 that designs and manufactures fully solid-state, high-resolution active electronically scanned array (AESA) phased-array radar systems built largely on commercial off-the-shelf hardware. Its products include the C-band GenRad GFC multi-mission AESA radar with a GaN front-end and digital beam-forming, and the Mark-IV 76-81GHz millimeter-wave 3D imaging radar producing LIDAR-like point clouds. The company serves aerospace and defense (U.S. Air Force, Navy, NORAD), counter-drone, airfield foreign-object-debris (FOD) detection, autonomy, wind energy, and weather markets, and has raised over $35M from investors including Kleiner Perkins and Octave Ventures. General Radar publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness.

providers.name: Generalastro
providers.description: General Astronautics (Generalastro) is a Y Combinator (W26) space-robotics company founded in 2025 by Bram Schork, based in San Francisco, building autonomous dexterous robotic arms that perform laboratory research and manufacturing tasks in microgravity without astronaut intervention. Its systems handle work like pipetting, sample prep, plate handling, and reagent mixing, targeting microgravity production of pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and fiber optics where crew time on orbital stations is the bottleneck (NASA estimates ISS crew time at ~$130K/hour). The company is pre-product hardware, backed by Y Combinator and Planet Ventures (~$7.1M raised), and currently exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface; this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Gilmour Space
providers.description: Gilmour Space Technologies is an Australian venture-backed space company headquartered on the Gold Coast in Queensland, founded in 2012 by brothers Adam and James Gilmour. The company designs and manufactures hybrid-propulsion orbital launch vehicles (the Eris rocket) and satellite platforms (the G-class / ElaraSat bus), and operates the Bowen Orbital Spaceport in North Queensland from which it is pursuing Australia's first sovereign orbital launch. Gilmour Space is backed by investors including Blackbird Ventures, Main Sequence Ventures, 500 Global, Fine Structure Ventures and HESTA. It is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the company operates in aerospace and space launch and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Hawaiian Holdings
providers.description: Hawaiian Holdings was the parent company of Hawaiian Airlines, the largest and longest-serving airline of Hawaii, providing scheduled passenger service to destinations across the Pacific. In 2024 the company combined with Alaska Air Group, and Hawaiian Holdings became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Alaska Air Group. No public developer portal or production-facing APIs are advertised.

providers.name: Hop Aero
providers.description: Hop Aero is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) aerospace and defense company based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2024 by Jacob Balaj and Matija Milenovic. The company develops hypersonic rocket cargo vehicles that deliver payloads point-to-point into austere, contested environments hundreds of miles away in minutes, aiming to give the United States and its allies an asymmetric logistics advantage. Hop Aero has raised a $3M pre-seed round and won a $1.25M U.S. Air Force SBIR award; its team draws on experience from SpaceX, Virgin Orbit, Masten Space Systems, SpinLaunch, and Destinus. This is a hardware-stage company with no public API or developer surface at the time of profiling; this record was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and is maintained for network discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Hypersonica
providers.description: Hypersonica is a European defence and aerospace company developing sovereign hypersonic strike systems for both military and civilian applications. Founded to give Europe an independent technological edge to deter aggression, the company tested what it describes as Europe's first sovereign hypersonic missile prototype in February 2026, focusing on fast, modular, maneuverable deep-strike capabilities delivered in months rather than years at a claimed 80% cost reduction. Headquartered in Munich with UK offices, Hypersonica raised a EUR 23.3M Series A backed by Plural, SPRIND, and General Catalyst. As a business-to-government defence contractor it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so no API artifacts could be enriched.

providers.name: Impossible Aerospace
providers.description: Impossible Aerospace is a deep-tech aerospace hardware company founded in 2016 by Spencer Gore in Santa Clara, California. It builds the US-1, a long-range all-electric quadcopter whose lithium-ion cells form part of the airframe structure, giving it up to roughly two hours of flight time for aerial imaging, surveillance, and public-safety missions with law enforcement and first responders. The US-1 runs the third-party Auterion OS flight stack (built on the PX4 open autopilot). The company was later acquired and operates as a small team. Enrichment note (2026-07-19): the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface, and its primary domain impossible.aero no longer resolves in DNS.

providers.name: Iridium
providers.description: Iridium Communications Inc. (NASDAQ: IRDM) is a McLean, Virginia satellite communications company operating a constellation of 66 cross-linked Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites that deliver truly global L-band voice, data, IoT, and positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) services across every region of the Earth, including the polar oceans. Iridium sells satellite phones (Iridium Extreme), satellite messengers, satellite IoT modules and modems (Iridium 9602/9603, Iridium Certus 9770/9810/9704, Iridium Edge, Iridium Edge Pro, Iridium Edge Solar), Short Burst Data (SBD) messaging, broadband Certus terminals, and next-generation Iridium NTN Direct 5G Non-Terrestrial Network services built on 3GPP NB-IoT for direct-to-device smartphone and IoT connectivity. Iridium CloudConnect — co-developed with Amazon Web Services — pipes satellite IoT data as JSON into customer-owned Amazon SQS queues inside their own AWS VPC over a dedicated private Iridium-AWS interconnect, making Iridium the first global cloud-native satellite IoT backhaul. The company serves aviation, maritime, government/defense, land-mobile, autonomous systems, and IoT markets through a partner ecosystem of more than 500 service providers, value-added resellers, and hardware OEMs, and in May 2026 announced a planned acquisition of Aireon, operator of the world's only space-based air traffic surveillance network. Iridium's business model is airtime/subscription revenue plus hardware module licensing and engineering services; there is no public, self-service developer API or OpenAPI — network access is mediated through Iridium-authorized service providers, the Iridium CloudConnect AWS integration, and hardware-level AT-command and SBD interfaces on Iridium modems.

providers.name: Iris Automation
providers.description: Iris Automation was a Reno, Nevada deep-tech company that built Casia, a computer-vision detect-and-avoid (DAA) system enabling beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) drone operations. Its onboard products (Casia, Casia X) and the ground-based Casia G used industrial cameras and machine-learning to detect non-cooperative intruder aircraft and prevent near mid-air collisions, integrating with MavLink-based autopilots and UAS ground control systems. Iris Automation was acquired by uAvionix in late 2023; the irisonboard.com domain now 301-redirects to uAvionix and the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or well-known surface of its own.

providers.name: Jjgmachining
providers.description: JJG (JJG Aero Pvt Ltd, JJG Machining Pvt Ltd, and JJG Special Processing Pvt Ltd) is a precision contract-manufacturing group founded in 2004 that produces machined components for the aerospace, automotive, and industrial sectors. It offers 2-5 axis CNC machining alongside high-volume turned and turn-mill parts in ferrous, aluminum, copper alloys, and titanium, backed by 30+ NADCAP-approved special processes such as electroplating, anodizing, paint, and NDT. This is a physical manufacturing company with no public API, developer program, or machine-readable API artifacts; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record only.

providers.name: K2 Space
providers.description: K2 Space (K2 Space Corporation) is a Los Angeles / Torrance, California aerospace startup that designs and manufactures high-power "Mega Class" satellite buses. Its platforms deliver roughly 20kW of array power and up to one metric ton of payload capacity - about ten times the power and payload of conventional buses - to maximize the throw-weight of next-generation launch vehicles like SpaceX Starship and Blue Origin New Glenn. K2 builds radiation-tolerant, vertically integrated (80% in-house) spacecraft with redundant avionics and high-delta-v propulsion for LEO, MEO, GEO and cislunar missions, serving commercial and U.S. government / defense customers. Backed by First Round Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Redpoint Ventures, the company raised a $250M Series C at a $3B valuation and is preparing its first production satellite, GRAVITAS. K2 Space is a hardware company with no public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Maquoketa Research
providers.description: Maquoketa Research is a defense-technology startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building autonomous terminal-guidance systems for one-way attack drones. Its platform-agnostic guidance modules add custom computer-vision object tracking to low-cost FPV drone hardware, raising strike success rates from under 25% to roughly 80% while maintaining target lock through GPS jamming and signal loss. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the five-person team ships hardware modules (product lines include GCS, Magpie, Odin, and TGS) that integrate with existing drone flight controllers rather than a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from the company's public website; it currently exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform surface.

providers.name: Nexus Lab Technologies, Inc.
providers.description: Nexus Lab (Nexus Lab Technologies, Inc.) is a contrail-reduction software company founded in 2022 and backed by 500 Global. Operating from nexuslab.fr, it applies machine learning to satellite imagery, flight traffic data, and meteorological parameters to help airlines optimize flight paths and reduce contrail formation, mitigating aviation's non-CO2 climate impact. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a marketing website with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; no developer surface was found to catalog.

providers.name: Noise & Vibration Technologies
providers.description: Noise & Vibration Technologies (NVT Group) is a Battery Ventures-backed platform of test-and-measurement companies that design, manufacture, and support equipment for measuring, simulating, and analyzing vibration, noise, shock, and other environmental variables. Its operating brands include Data Physics (SignalCalc dynamic signal analyzers and vibration controllers), Team Corporation (electrodynamic and hydraulic shakers), and Lansmont (package and product-testing systems), serving aerospace, defense, commercial space, automotive, and industrial customers worldwide. The company ships hardware and desktop analysis/control software rather than any public web API, REST service, SDK, or developer portal, so it has no programmable API surface for the API Evangelist network at this time.

providers.name: Orbital ATK
providers.description: Orbital ATK was an American aerospace manufacturer and defense industry company formed in February 2015 by the merger of Orbital Sciences Corporation and the defense and aerospace divisions of Alliant Techsystems. The company produced launch vehicles, satellites, missiles, ammunition, precision-guided munitions, rocket motors, and the Cygnus spacecraft for ISS resupply before being acquired by Northrop Grumman on June 6, 2018 and rebranded as Northrop Grumman Innovation Systems.

providers.name: Ornadyne
providers.description: Ornadyne is a Los Angeles hard-tech startup building autonomous flapping-wing UAVs (ornithopters) that look and fly like real birds for covert reconnaissance and surveillance. Its near-silent, AI-powered, man-portable drones are engineered for low acoustic and visual signatures, hour-class flight times, and natural bird-like flight, contrasting with easily detected quadcopters and fixed-wing aircraft. Founded by Geourg Kivijian (CEO, ex-NASA JPL and Astrolab) and Armen Arakelyan (CTO, ex-SpaceX Starship), the company is a Y Combinator Spring 2026 company operating in the hardware, robotics, drones, aerospace, and defense space. It is a hardware/defense company with a marketing website and no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Performance Drone Works
providers.description: Performance Drone Works is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of lux-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: defense. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Pratt & Whitney
providers.description: A major American aerospace manufacturer designing, manufacturing, and servicing aircraft engines for commercial, military, and business aviation applications. A division of RTX Corporation (formerly Raytheon Technologies), Pratt & Whitney is known for its geared turbofan (GTF) engine technology (PW1000G family) powering the Airbus A220 and A320neo, the F135 powering the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter, and the PT6 turboprop family. Customer-facing digital services - EngineWise health monitoring, FAST (Full-flight data Acquisition Storage and Transmission), and the Customer Portal - are operated privately for airline, MRO, and military customers behind credentialed access and are not exposed as a public developer API or open partner integration portal.

providers.name: Precision Castparts
providers.description: Precision Castparts Corp. is a worldwide manufacturer of complex metal components and products including investment castings, forgings, and fasteners and structurals for aerospace and industrial gas turbine markets. The company is owned by Berkshire Hathaway.

providers.name: Raphe Mphibr
providers.description: Raphe mPhibr is an Indian deep-tech aerospace company revolutionizing unmanned aviation through in-house carbon fiber composites, UAV airframes, propulsion, and end-to-end manufacturing. The company designs and builds heavy-lift and tactical unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs/drones) for defense and industrial applications, emphasizing research-driven innovation and vertically integrated production. Raphe mPhibr is a B2B / defense-oriented manufacturer surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface — its digital presence is a corporate marketing site only.

providers.name: Rocket Lab
providers.description: Rocket Lab (Rocket Lab Corporation, formerly Rocket Lab USA; Nasdaq RKLB) is an American aerospace manufacturer and end-to-end space company founded in 2006 by Peter Beck. It designs and launches the Electron small-lift orbital rocket, is developing the reusable Neutron medium-lift vehicle, and builds the Photon spacecraft platform along with satellites, spacecraft components, solar cells, reaction wheels, star trackers, separation systems and other space systems. Rocket Lab operates launch complexes in Mahia, New Zealand and at Wallops Island, Virginia, providing dedicated and rideshare launch services plus on-orbit management for commercial, civil and national-security customers. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Khosla Ventures; this profile is enriched from public identity and live domain probes only, as Rocket Lab publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Singularity
providers.description: Singularity (Singularity Defense Corp) is a defense-technology company building low-cost, mass-producible air-defense and counter-weapon systems to protect warfighters and civilians from drones and cheap aerial munitions. Founded by engineers from SpaceX, Tesla, and Anduril alongside operators who have deployed air defenses in combat, the company emerged from stealth in July 2026 with an $80M Series A at a $400M valuation led by Khosla Ventures and Felicis, with Menlo Ventures, NEA, Y Combinator, Harpoon Ventures, and others participating. It emphasizes in-house manufacturing of major subsystems combined with commercial-volume components for rapid production and field deployment, including active conflict zones. Singularity is a hardware defense company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio lead and enriched with verified company identity by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Singularity Defense
providers.description: Singularity Defense Corp (operating on singularityus.com) is a defense-technology company building affordable, scalable counter-weapon air defense systems that protect warfighters and civilians from drones and low-cost, mass-produced munitions. Led by CEO Jack Oswald with COO Shail Giroux, the company is backed by Khosla Ventures, New Enterprise Associates, Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, Menlo Ventures, and Felicis. It ships physical air-defense hardware and publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; this enrichment pass confirmed the company has no public API surface.

providers.name: SpinLaunch
providers.description: SpinLaunch is a space technology company developing a kinetic launch system that uses a rotating carbon-fiber arm inside a large vacuum chamber to accelerate launch vehicles to thousands of kilometers per hour before ignition, aiming to eliminate up to 70 percent of the fuel and structure of a conventional rocket. It operates a Suborbital Accelerator test facility at Spaceport America in New Mexico that doubles as a customer payload-testing platform, and is developing an Orbital Launch System alongside its Meridian satellite broadband constellation for enterprise connectivity. Backed by GV, the company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Target Arm
providers.description: Target Arm is a robotics company building systems to autonomously launch and recover drones from moving vehicles without stopping. Its Ralar robotic arm captures drones mid-air, recharges them, and relaunches them, while TRACKR sensor-fusion, TurboFly autopilot, and Maestro mission-control software coordinate drone fleets across commercial delivery, first-responder, agriculture, energy-inspection, and defense/ISR use cases. A Techstars-backed hardware startup with no public API or developer program at this time; this network profile captures identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: Tenet Industries
providers.description: Tenet Industries is a Swedish defense-technology startup founded in 2026 by Hugo Frisk, Fabian Andersson, and Emil Falk (students from KTH Royal Institute of Technology and the Stockholm School of Economics) building low-cost, mass-producible defense systems. Applying design-for-manufacturing and first-principles engineering, the company starts with strike/attack drones — a kamikaze quadcopter that assembles in two minutes with roughly half the parts of comparable systems — and extends the same hardware/software platform to loitering munitions, jammers, radars, and missile systems. Backed by Y Combinator ($500K). As a defense hardware manufacturer, Tenet Industries currently publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Venus Aerospace
providers.description: Venus Aerospace is a propulsion company building the Venus Rotating Detonation Rocket Engine (RDRE) and the Venus Detonation Ramjet (VDR), a hybrid that pairs the RDRE with air-breathing ramjet technology to carry a vehicle from takeoff through hypersonic cruise on a single engine. The company positions detonation-based propulsion — supersonic detonation waves propagating around an annular combustor rather than conventional subsonic combustion — for defense munitions and uncrewed systems, space upper stages, orbital transfer vehicles and landers, and commercial high-speed flight. Venus Aerospace is a hardware and flight-test organization: it publishes a public marketing site covering the RDRE, the VDR, its team, investors and newsroom, but no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: VeriTX
providers.description: VeriTX Corp. is a veteran-owned blockchain and cybersecurity firm based in East Aurora, New York that builds trusted, tamper-evident data and supply-chain infrastructure originally developed for the U.S. Air Force under SBIR, STTR, and Defense Production Act programs. Its flagship product, QuDEFENSE, is a data-security platform that combines post-quantum cryptography with blockchain to protect sensitive files in transit and at rest, providing real-time manipulation detection, automatic quarantine of tampered data, immutable audit trails, and end-to-end data provenance. VeriTX began as a blockchain-powered digital marketplace for aerospace additive manufacturing (3D-printed aircraft parts) built on Algorand, and has since focused on secure data transfer and provenance for defense, aerospace, medical, and industrial customers. QuDEFENSE is offered as an API, an Outlook plugin, and a standalone web interface, though VeriTX does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: Vertical Circuits
providers.description: Vertical Circuits, Inc. (VCI) was a semiconductor company based in Scotts Valley, California, supplying high-density semiconductor memories and die-level vertical-interconnect packaging technology. Its patented ViP (vertical interconnect pillar) process stacked die to bridge wire-bond product solutions and through-silicon-via (TSV) technology, serving computer, telecom, consumer-electronics, aerospace, and military customers. The company's die-stacking IP and technology were acquired by Invensas/Tessera around 2013. Vertical Circuits is a hardware and semiconductor-IP company with no public web API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; it was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead and enriched to record that it has no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Virgin Galactic
providers.description: Virgin Galactic is a publicly traded (NYSE: SPCE) commercial spaceflight company founded by Richard Branson that develops and operates suborbital, crewed spaceplanes for space tourism and research payloads. It flies its air-launched SpaceShipTwo-class and next generation Delta-class vehicles from Spaceport America in New Mexico, carrying private astronauts and scientific experiments to the edge of space. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Social Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface: it is a consumer-facing space-tourism business, not an API provider.

providers.name: Lockheed Martin
providers.description: Lockheed Martin is a leading global security, defense, and aerospace contractor. This repository captures the public APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts where they exist for Lockheed Martin.

providers.name: GE Aerospace
providers.description: A leading manufacturer of jet engines and aviation systems for commercial and military aircraft. Spun off from General Electric to focus exclusively on aerospace propulsion and services, GE Aerospace also offers software-as-a-service tooling, engine health monitoring (Collaborative Insight), TRUEngine certification, and OnPoint maintenance and support services.

providers.name: Vector Launch
providers.description: Vector Launch, Inc. (originally Vector Space Systems) was an American small-launch and space software company founded in February 2016 in Tucson, Arizona by Jim Cantrell — an early SpaceX executive — with John Garvey, Shaun Coleman, Ken Sunshine and Eric Besnard. It acquired Garvey Spacecraft in July 2016 and developed two LOX/propylene micro-launch vehicles, the Vector-R and the larger Vector-H, aimed at a high-cadence smallsat launch market, alongside GalacticSky, a San Jose based software-defined-satellite platform that produced more than forty patents and was marketed in 2016 with a promised suite of satellite SDKs, APIs and a satellite-optimised Linux distribution called GalacticOS. Those developer surfaces were announced but never shipped publicly: Vector operated no developer portal, published no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL or Postman collection, ran no public GitHub organisation, and distributed no client SDK to any package registry. The company raised roughly $22M disclosed (a $1M angel round from Shaun Coleman, then $21M in June 2017 from Sequoia Capital, Shasta Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners), flew suborbital prototypes from Mojave and Spaceport Camden, and won a $3.4M U.S. Air Force ASLON-45 mission in August 2019 that was cancelled days later on solvency grounds. Sequoia withdrew support in August 2019, Cantrell departed, operations halted, and Vector filed Chapter 11 in Delaware on 13 December 2019; Lockheed Martin took the GalacticSky assets by default for $4.25M when no qualified competing bid appeared, and a separate bidder took the launch-vehicle assets. A relaunched entity under Robert Spalding re-emerged on 29 October 2020, shareholders voted a wind-down in January 2021, and the residual business was finally absorbed on 26 February 2026 when Phantom Space — Jim Cantrell's later company — acquired Vector's remaining assets, engineering data, tooling and intellectual property to accelerate its Daytona launch vehicle. Nothing of Vector's own web presence survives: vector-launch.com is a dormant GoDaddy-registered holding domain that fails TLS name validation and returns 404 on every path, and the earlier vectorspacesystems.com brand domain lapsed and now redirects off-domain to an unrelated gambling site. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: General Electric
providers.description: General Electric Company has reorganized into separate publicly traded companies: GE Aerospace, focused on jet engines and aviation systems, and GE Vernova, focused on energy and power generation. GE HealthCare was spun off in 2023. No unified public developer API portal is currently published by GE Aerospace or GE Vernova.

providers.name: RedWing Aerospace Laboratories
providers.description: RedWing Aerospace Laboratories (RedWing Labs, operated by Kitemaps AMS Pvt Ltd) is a Bangalore, India based, Techstars-backed company that designs, develops and deploys fully autonomous drones to transform logistics supply chains. It offers a fleet of long-range, urban and medium-range delivery aircraft plus an operations software suite, and runs an autonomous four-step delivery flow (order, handoff to flight operations, proof of delivery, return to hub) used to move healthcare products, food and other goods within the hour. The company reports operational milestones including 145,930+ kilometers flown and thousands of deliveries completed. RedWing does not publish a first-party developer API; its public agent surface is the platform-provided Wix Site MCP endpoint advertised in its llms.txt.

providers.name: Parker Hannifin
providers.description: Parker Hannifin is a global leader in motion and control technologies, providing precision-engineered solutions for a wide variety of mobile, industrial, and aerospace markets. No public developer API has been documented at this time.

providers.name: Raytheon
providers.description: Raytheon is an American aerospace and defense manufacturer operating as a business of RTX Corporation, the world's largest aerospace and defense company. Raytheon designs, develops, and produces advanced defense systems including precision weapons, air and missile defense systems, sensors, radar, electronic warfare, command-and-control solutions, and cyber capabilities for the U.S. military and allied governments worldwide. Key products include the Patriot missile defense system, StormBreaker smart weapons, RAIVEN electro-optical/infrared sensor suites, and advanced electronic attack systems. Raytheon also develops world-class logistics software through the EAGLE team supporting production management, technical manual development, and product support data. No public developer API or machine-readable specification is available at this time; Raytheon's software solutions are deployed within government program contracts.

providers.name: Accion Systems
providers.description: Accion Systems is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of shasta-ventures, slow-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: aerospace. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: ATI
providers.description: ATI Inc. is a specialty materials and components manufacturer that produces high-performance alloys, titanium products, nickel-based superalloys, and engineered components. The company primarily serves the aerospace, defense, energy, electronics, and medical industries. ATI focuses on direct B2B customer relationships and does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: Exelis
providers.description: Exelis Inc. was an American global aerospace, defense, information, and services company that produced communications systems, electronic warfare products, geospatial systems, integrated structures, and night vision equipment. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, Exelis was acquired by Harris Corporation in 2015. Harris and L3 Technologies then merged in 2019 to form L3Harris Technologies. No public APIs are published under the Exelis brand; developer resources, if any, are tracked under L3Harris.

providers.name: Howmet Aerospace
providers.description: Howmet Aerospace is a global leader in advanced engineered solutions for the aerospace and transportation industries, providing engine components, fastening systems, engineered structures, and forged wheels.

providers.name: IDEX Corporation
providers.description: IDEX Corporation (NYSE: IEX) is a global engineered products company that designs and manufactures pumps, flow meters, valves, fluidics systems, precision components, and fire and safety equipment. IDEX serves health, science, water, energy, semiconductor, aerospace, fire and safety, and industrial markets through three segments: Fluid and Metering Technologies, Health and Science Technologies, and Fire and Safety / Diversified Products.

providers.name: Samara Aerospace
providers.description: Samara Aerospace is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of techstars and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Kyten Technologies
providers.description: Kyten Technologies is a Seattle, Washington hardware manufacturing startup building a factory to produce custom aerospace-grade battery packs. The founders spent six years at Starlink, where they put more than 5,000 battery packs into space, and are now bringing rapid development and volume production of aerospace-grade battery packs to the wider industry. The company positions itself against a legacy supply chain that cannot keep up with the 100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites being built in the United States. Kyten Technologies is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, classified under Industrials / Manufacturing and Robotics, and was an early-stage two-person team at the time of profiling. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Allegiant Travel
providers.description: Allegiant Travel Company is a leisure-focused U.S. airline holding company and a Fortune 1000 firm operating Allegiant Air, which provides low-cost, mostly nonstop flights between underserved cities and popular leisure destinations. The company also bundles air travel with hotels, rental cars, and event tickets through its allegiant.com booking platform. Allegiant does not publish a public developer portal or external API.

providers.name: L-3 Communications
providers.description: L-3 Communications was a U.S. defense prime contractor specializing in command, control, communications, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C3ISR) systems, aircraft modernization and maintenance, and government services. In 2019 L-3 merged with Harris Corporation to form L3Harris Technologies, which continues the legacy product lines and is now ranked among the top U.S. defense contractors. No public developer API has been documented.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Nabhdrishti Aerospace
providers.description: Nabhdrishti Aerospace is a Bangalore-based deep-tech startup building India's first fuel-flex micro gas turbine for aviation and power generation. Its ND 400 engine is a 400 N single-core micro gas turbine designed for UAVs, hybrid-electric aircraft, and small aircraft as well as oil & gas, manufacturing, and vehicle range-extender power generation, running on conventional fuels, biofuels, and hydrogen with an innovative recuperator design that targets greater than 15% efficiency at under half the cost of competing turbines. Backed by Accel, the company raised USD 3M and operates from the IISc Bangalore IHUB. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks its public web presence.

providers.name: Plexus
providers.description: Plexus is a global manufacturing and product development company that helps customers in highly regulated industries (Aerospace/Defense, Healthcare/Life Sciences, Industrial, and Semiconductor Capital Equipment) design, manufacture, and service their products. Plexus does not currently publish a public developer API; this index tracks customer/supplier portals and corporate web properties.

providers.name: JetBlue Airways
providers.description: JetBlue Airways is a low-cost airline that operates flights to destinations across the United States, Caribbean, Latin America, and Europe, known for its customer service and inflight amenities.

providers.name: BBN Technologies
providers.description: BBN Technologies is a research and development organization founded in 1948 (originally Bolt Beranek and Newman) and now operating as RTX BBN Technologies, a division of RTX (Raytheon). BBN is historically notable for pioneering the ARPANET, early network email, and packet-switched networking, and today conducts advanced defense and intelligence R&D across AI/machine learning, command and control, cyber operations, signal processing and spectrum, networking, quantum and photonics, and voice and language technologies. BBN serves government and defense customers and does not publish a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface; this profile is maintained for network identity and discovery only.

providers.name: Benchmark Electronics
providers.description: Benchmark Electronics, Inc. is an advanced electronics engineering and manufacturing services (EMS) company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. The company provides integrated design, engineering, and manufacturing services from prototypes to high-volume production, including procurement, logistics, and repair. Benchmark serves original equipment manufacturers in defense, medical technologies, commercial aerospace, industrial, next-gen communications, advanced computing, and semiconductor capital equipment markets. The company operates approximately 22 locations in 8 countries with around 13,000 employees.

providers.name: Beyond Reach Labs
providers.description: Beyond Reach Labs is a Brooklyn, New York aerospace company building deployable solar arrays and thermal radiators for spacecraft that expand from compact launch sizes to enormous structures in orbit. Its patented geometry-changing panels grow from the size of a dining table to a football field once deployed, giving satellites, orbital data centers, commercial space stations, and lunar outposts up to 10x more usable power without adding launch mass or volume. Founded by two aerospace engineers, the company is targeting its first in-space demonstration in Q2 2027 and is a Y Combinator portfolio company. Beyond Reach Labs is a hardware manufacturer and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Curtiss-Wright
providers.description: Curtiss-Wright is a global integrated business that provides highly engineered products, solutions, and services mainly to the aerospace, defense, commercial power, process, and general industrial markets. Its product portfolio spans rugged embedded computing, mission-critical avionics, electronic packaging, naval propulsion, reactor coolant pumps for nuclear power, surface treatment services, industrial valves, sensors, data acquisition systems, telemetry ground stations, emergency arresting systems for military aircraft, and electronic systems for naval shipbuilding programs. The company traces its lineage to the aviation pioneers Glenn Curtiss and the Wright brothers and today operates across the Defense Electronics, Naval & Power, and Aerospace & Industrial segments.

providers.name: Icarus
providers.description: Icarus is an aerospace and defense company building autonomous, solar-powered stratospheric aircraft for persistent surveillance and connectivity. Its APOLLO platform operates continuously above 60,000 feet, delivering rapid aerial intelligence, wide-area coverage across 1,000+ square miles, and always-on, low-latency (5-10ms) direct-to-device communications for weeks-long missions without ground infrastructure. Founded in 2023 and based in El Segundo, California, Icarus was part of Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch.
